biggest_catch: The annual fee eats the bonus: the $95 fee is $0 in year one, so the full $300 is net-positive in year one — but from year two on, the year-one-style math is $300 minus $95 = $205 net, and only if you were already going to spend $3,000 in six months. Your offer may also be less than the $300 max.
catches: Only claim this bonus if you were ALREADY going to spend $3,000 in six months — never spend extra to chase a bonus.
The annual fee eats the bonus: $0 intro annual fee for the first year, then $95 — year-one net is the full $300 you qualify for; from year two the math is $300 minus $95.
The offer is 'as high as' $300 — Amex tells you your exact amount during the application and it may be lower.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry.
Once-per-lifetime rule: no welcome offer if you have or have had this Card, the Morgan Stanley Blue Cash Preferred, or previous versions.
Amex's eligibility check can deny the welcome offer based on your history (balance transfers, Card Member history, cards opened/closed); you are notified before processing so you can withdraw.
Carrying a balance at ~20%+ APR wipes out the bonus instantly — pay in full (note the 0% intro APR for 12 months tempts carrying a balance; don't).

Fees, interest, balance transfers, cash advances, gift cards, prepaid reloads, and person-to-person payments do not count toward the $3,000 threshold; account must not be past due or cancelled when Reward Dollars post.

steps: Apply for the Blue Cash Preferred Card on the official Amex page — not from an affiliate link with different terms.
During the application Amex tells you the exact cash-back amount you qualify for (as high as $300); withdraw if shown no offer.
If approved, make $3,000 in eligible purchases you were already planning within the first 6 months of Card Membership.
Pay the balance in full every month — do not let the 0% intro APR tempt you into carrying a balance.
Keep the account open, not past due; the Reward Dollars post 8-12 weeks after you hit $3,000.
Redeem the Reward Dollars as a statement credit (or at Amazon.com checkout).
